features.name: Deck list and empty-set state
steps: First launch with no decks
Show "Collection is empty"
After creating/importing the first deck the empty state disappears
The deck list shows names and derived counts such as new/learning/review
After deleting the last deck the empty-collection state returns
features.expected: The new, learning, and review counts must be derived from the real card states rather than hard-coded or stale; the empty-set message appears only when there is no deck; after deleting the last deck the app must return to the empty state rather than a blank page.

features.name: Create a normal deck
steps: Tap the "+" in the bottom-right corner
Expand the action menu
Select "Create deck"
Enter a name
An empty name cannot create a deck
After confirming, the new deck immediately joins the deck list
The deck still exists after leaving the page or restarting
features.expected: Empty or duplicate names must be rejected with a prompt; after a successful creation the new deck immediately appears in the list with a count of 0; the deck must be written to the collection database and still exist after leaving or restarting.

features.name: Deck lifecycle and hierarchy
steps: An existing deck
Rename the deck
The card associations stay unchanged
Create a subdeck/hierarchical relationship
The parent deck aggregates the subdeck data

After deleting a deck the related lists and counts update in sync and other decks are unaffected. The official documentation supports lifecycle operations such as deck renaming, subdecks, and deletion.
features.expected: Renaming only changes the name and must not lose card associations; the cards of a subdeck should count toward the parent deck's totals; after deleting a deck its cards are transferred or handled according to the rules, and other decks' counts are unaffected.

features.name: Add a note to a specified deck
steps: From "+"
Add, or enter the add screen from the specified deck
Choose the deck and note type
Enter fields such as Front/Back
Tags/media can be added
Save
Cards are generated according to the note type and assigned to the target deck
Deck counts change in sync.
features.expected: After saving, the corresponding number of cards must be generated according to the note type and assigned to the selected deck; empty required fields cannot be saved; new cards must count toward that deck's "new" count and persist.

features.name: One-to-many generation between notes and cards
steps: Creating a note with an ordinary type such as "Basic" generates ordinary cards
Switching to a type such as "Basic (and reversed card)" lets the same note generate cards in multiple directions
After modifying the note fields, all cards generated from it use the latest content in sync rather than being copied into multiple independent text objects
features.expected: The cards generated by one note must share the same field data, and after editing the note all card contents update in sync; deleting a note should delete all its cards; the number of cards is defined by the template rather than created manually.

features.name: Note type selection and management
steps: Open "Note types"
Show types such as image occlusion, cloze, basic, optional reversed, type-in answer, and basic-and-reversed, along with their note counts
After adding/editing a note type, it can be selected when creating a new note
The type configuration is persisted
features.expected: Each note type must show its real associated note count; a newly added type must appear in the note-type list when adding notes; changes to type fields and templates should affect the generation and display of the corresponding cards and persist.

features.name: Edit notes and card membership
steps: Open an existing note from the card browser or the review screen
Edit fields/tags
Save
The browser and review pages show the new content in sync
After moving the card to another deck both deck counts are recalculated
It is still preserved after re-entering
features.expected: Edited content must be written back to the note itself rather than to a card copy, and the browser and review screens read from the same data source; after moving a card the source and target deck counts update in sync; changes must persist.

features.name: Basic study flow
steps: Open a deck with cards to study
Show the question side
Use "Show answer"
Show the answer side and the answer buttons
Choose the answer result
Move to the next card
After study completes, return to the completion/deck state rather than looping the same card forever
features.expected: Answer buttons must not appear and answers must not be recorded before the answer is shown; after each answer the card must leave the current queue; when the queue is exhausted a completion state is shown and the deck's remaining counts update, without the same card appearing repeatedly.

features.name: Again / Hard / Good / Easy scheduling
steps: Choose "Again / Hard / Good / Easy" for the same card
The card's next review time changes differently depending on the answer
The answer buttons can show the next interval
When due, the card re-enters the pending-review queue. The official documentation makes clear that the answer buttons affect when the card appears again.
features.expected: The next intervals produced by the four buttons must differ, with Again shortest and Easy longest; when due again the card must re-enter the review queue; the scheduling result must persist into the collection.

features.name: Card learning lifecycle
steps: A new card is studied for the first time
It enters learning
After meeting the graduation condition it enters the review state
After a lapse it enters relearning
Different intervals/ease values form over time and with review performance
The new/learning/review counts on the deck home page are always derived in real time from these card states
features.expected: Card states (new, learning, review, relearning) must be driven by the actual answer history; each state's count reflects the current collection in real time and the total is conserved; state changes must persist across restarts.

features.name: Card operations during review
steps: During study, cards can be flagged, buried, suspended, edited, or the last answer can be undone
A buried card does not appear again today but recovers afterwards
A suspended card stays excluded until the suspension is manually cancelled
Undo restores the scheduling state from before the answer rather than only toggling the UI.
features.expected: Bury must take effect the same day and recover automatically the next day; suspend must last until manually cancelled; Undo must roll back the scheduling and counts rather than only the display; each flag state must persist and not interfere with the others.

features.name: Review sessions and time settings
steps: Set "next day starts at", "learn ahead limit", "limit study duration", "keep screen on", etc.
Return to study
The new time boundaries and session rules apply to subsequent study
Configuration persists across pages and restarts
features.expected: The next-day start time must affect the "due today" boundary; when the study-duration limit is reached, further study should stop; the learn-ahead limit must change the review queue content; configuration must persist across restarts.

features.name: Card browser and complex search
steps: Open the "Card browser"
Select the current deck or all decks
Enter a query
Results change according to the search expression
Supports conditions such as is:due, tags, and fields
Open a result to edit it
After returning, the search context is still usable. The official documentation confirms that the browser supports complex Anki search expressions.
features.expected: Search results must be filtered from real cards by the query expression in real time and must not return the whole collection; results change when the deck scope is switched; after editing and returning, the original query and list position should be preserved.

features.name: Browser sorting and batch state
steps: In the card browser, view or sort by properties such as "sort field / card template / due / deck"
Select multiple cards
Perform operations such as flag or suspend on the selected set
The list state and deck statistics update in sync while unselected cards stay unchanged
features.expected: Sorting must genuinely change the list order; batch operations must only affect the selected items while unselected cards keep their state; deck statistics must update accordingly and persist after the operation.

features.name: Create a filtered deck
steps: Create a filtered deck
Set a name
Enter a query such as deck:Default is:due
Set a limit such as 100
Choose a sort mode such as random
A second filter can be enabled
Create
Only cards that match the conditions enter the temporary deck. The filter parameters in the screenshot are consistent with the official filtered-deck mechanism.
features.expected: A filtered deck can only contain cards that match the query and do not exceed the limit; the sort mode must affect card order; invalid queries or empty results must give feedback; the created result must persist.

features.name: Filtered deck lifecycle
steps: Create a filtered deck
The card keeps its original deck identity while temporarily entering the filtered deck
After studying in the filtered deck it is rescheduled according to the configuration
Empty/Rebuild recomputes the members
After deleting or emptying the filtered deck the cards return to their original deck and must not be deleted or copied.
features.expected: Cards must keep their original deck membership: a filtered deck only creates temporary references; Empty/Rebuild must recompute the members under the current conditions; deleting a filtered deck must not delete cards, and the cards must return to their original deck.

features.name: Statistics panel and time/scope filtering
steps: Open statistics
Select "deck/collection" and a time range
Today, forecast, calendar, review count, card count, review interval, card ease, retention, answer buttons, added, and other statistics are all recomputed over the same filter range
After completing new reviews the corresponding statistics change with the data
features.expected: All statistics must be recomputed for the selected deck and time range, and the numbers change in sync when the range changes; after new reviews are completed the corresponding charts and counts update immediately and must not show static sample data.

features.name: New study screen configuration
steps: Enable/disable the "new study screen"
Configure showing answer feedback, remaining card count, audio play button, answer buttons, toolbar position, etc.
After entering the study page the layout and controls change according to the settings
Card data and scheduling are unaffected by the visual configuration
features.expected: Toggles and options must genuinely change the layout and control visibility of the study screen; the configuration must persist; regardless of UI changes, card content, answer results, and scheduling must stay consistent.

features.name: Appearance and study-screen configuration
steps: Change theme / day theme / night theme / background
Adjust full screen, centering, top bar, remaining count, remaining time, deck title, audio button, etc.
After returning to study/browser the UI applies immediately
The configuration is persisted
features.expected: Theme and layout options must apply immediately to the study and browser screens; day and night themes take effect separately according to the system light/dark setting; the configuration persists across restarts and does not change card data.

features.name: Gestures, keyboard, and answer mapping
steps: Enable gestures under "Controls"
Change the swipe sensitivity
View/configure keyboard and controller shortcuts
While studying, use keys to trigger Show Answer or Again/Hard/Good/Easy
Produce the same scheduling result as tapping the buttons
features.expected: Keys and gestures must map to the corresponding answer actions and produce the same scheduling result as tapping the button; after gestures are disabled, swiping must no longer change the answer; the mapping configuration must persist.

features.name: Local backup and restore
steps: Generate periodic collection backups according to the "automatic backup interval"
Clean up old backups according to the daily/weekly/monthly retention count
The user can also "create a backup" manually
Modify or delete data

After selecting "restore backup", the cards, decks, and study data from the backup point in time are restored. The official documentation states that automatic backups include cards and statistics but not media files.
features.expected: Backup files must be genuinely created and old files cleaned up according to the retention count; after a restore, cards, decks, and review statistics must return to the backup point in time; media is outside the backup scope and must not be faked after a restore.

features.name: Import a deck package (.apkg)
steps: Menu
"Import deck"
Select "Deck package (.apkg)"
Select a valid file
Parse the decks/notes/cards inside it
Merge them into the existing collection
The new deck appears in the list
Unrelated existing decks must remain rather than the whole collection being overwritten. The official documentation distinguishes the merge behavior of deck packages
features.expected: Importing must merge rather than overwrite the existing collection, and existing decks and study data stay unchanged; the counts of imported decks, notes, and cards must match the file; a corrupted or non-.apkg file must produce an error without damaging the existing collection.

features.name: Import a collection (.colpkg)
steps: Menu
Import
"Collection file (.colpkg)"
Select the file
Confirm the behavior of overwriting the entire collection
After the import completes, decks, notes, review history, statistics, etc. all become the imported collection's data
It must not be wrongly merged like a normal .apkg. The official documentation makes clear that Collection Package and Deck Package have different semantics
features.expected: Before importing, the user must be warned that the whole collection will be overwritten and must confirm; after the import, decks, notes, review history, and statistics all become the file's data and the old data is no longer kept; cancelling or failing must not damage the original collection.

features.name: Import .txt / .csv text cards
steps: Import
"Text file (.txt, .csv)"
Select the UTF-8 text
Detect or choose the delimiter
Choose the Note Type and the target Deck
Map the file columns to fields such as Front/Back/Tags
Choose how duplicate notes are handled
Import
Each valid record generates a corresponding Note/Card. The current AnkiDroid upstream materials already cover text import, field mapping, and duplicate handling.
features.expected: The field mapping must determine which field the content is written into, and a wrong mapping must not be imported silently; duplicate notes must be skipped or merged according to the selected strategy; each valid record should generate a corresponding note and card and count toward the target deck.

features.name: Deck / collection export and reversible restore
steps: Export a single deck or export the collection from the main menu
Choose an Anki export format
You can select "include media files" and "support older Anki versions" as shown in the screenshot
Produce an actual export file
Import it again in a clean environment
Decks, notes, cards, and the selected data that was carried can be restored
When media is not included, media must not be falsely restored.
features.expected: The export must produce a real file that can be imported again; after re-importing, decks, notes, cards, and the selected review data must match the exported state; when media is not selected, no media content may appear after restoring.
